Both sides are asked the bill and the weight, the taming rule in the same words, that an occupied crate goes nowhere but down on the ground, setting it down and picking it up with the wildermon in it, letting it out to follow you or to work, that a worker taken off the deed leaves the companion in its place, and where a young one is born; the island also that your own crated wildermon come down from anywhere, and the browser that an old save's kept-at-token wildermon get a crate.

title: A new look, worn on an island
why: "allow players to change their appearance back through the customizer in Settings". The window is the account page's creator; on an island it wears a look through `Island.wearLook`. This asks, against a keeper stubbed on fetch, that the look goes to rpc_set_look whole, that what is worn is what the keeper kept, that a body standing still still broadcasts it, and that a refusal changes nothing.

title: Looks for the sculpted bodies, the same on both sides
why: "revamp the character customization screen for the new models. It will only have the 2 body types, 3 hairstyles (2+bald). It needs sliders for hair color and skin tone." The bodies and the hairstyles there is a mesh for; the skin, hair colour and grey as numbers clamped to nought to one; every old id to the nearest of now; look_clean as cleanLook; the doors, the old rows rewritten.

title: Bodies go to the blocks round you, not to the whole island
why: A body, a wave and a cast go out on the topic of the block their sender stands in and are heard on the nine round you, so the messages a second are the people near you and not the square of everybody on the island. Nine held mid-island, four in a corner; the next block heard, two off not held; a walk keeps six, leaves three, joins three; a topic let go of is not heard.

title: A kept thing stays kept
why: Reported: "Something is unlocking my supreme mortars over and over." Of every action asked of a kept pile only Unlock unlocks it; a part or the whole of one moved into a bag and back stays kept (`move_part`), a pile kept while the pack is folded is not folded (`pack_fold`), and in the browser an older answer arriving after a newer one does not put the kept pile back as loose (`Island.act`).

title: One pile and not six
why: Reported off a screenshot of a pack holding six separate piles of cotton seeds. `give` had always folded a harvest into a matching stack; the eight statements that *move* a row into a pack folded nothing, so every one of them started a rival pile. One rule now, `stack_key`, with `sameStack` in the browser saying the same thing — which this asks pair by pair rather than trusting.

title: Talk kept apart and kept longer
why: Reported: the Talk tab emptied once enough lines of any kind came in, a worker's run of work lines among them. The browser keeps talk apart now (`trimLog`), and the island keeps chat three days and hands back as many lines as the browser keeps.

title: Deploy a carried vehicle beside you
why: Asked for: Deploy on a carried wagon, set down at once rather than steered like furniture. The spot is `place_furniture`'s own: off your tile, within reach, turned the way you face.

title: Sprouts, none off a sapling and one a tree an hour
why: Reported: sprouts picked off saplings. A stage with no timber has none, and a pick marks the tree for `sprout_cooldown`, workers too.

title: Packed dirt is not raised by Change tile
why: Reported: packed dirt could not be flattened and could be raised with Change tile. Both Change tiles refuse it, on both sides.

title: What gathering gives, and when a spot is ready again
why: A spot picked over says the wait to the second on both sides, the browser reading `foraged`; odds, ceilings and seasons on the menus and the tile window are the island's numbers.

title: A slab is floor for everything on it
why: Reported: a wagon and an altar drawn on the ground under a slab, and a body swimming on one poured in water. Its top holds up whatever is on it, on both sides; a pool dug in it is water.

title: A worker that can reach the larder
why: `worker_feed` looked in crates and nowhere else, so a wildermon could stand beside a larder holding a hundred and fifty of exactly what it eats and starve. The browser never had that fault. This asks both halves: every store on the deed is somewhere to look, and a locked stack, priced stock, post and goods under a deal are not lunch — none of which were checked before.

title: Fourteen trades, and one of them yours
why: Sixty-one skills and no way of saying what you *are*. A class is that: fourteen craft trades, one locked in, opening at fifty in any skill it covers, free the first time and 500 silver to swap. This asks both sides for the list and adds it up — every craft skill in exactly one trade, and what is left over exactly the twenty-two the combat trades will be drawn from, so no skill gates two cards.

title: Nine nodes to a trade
why: Three columns of three per trade, two points at fifty and twelve at a hundred — so twelve buys two whole columns and two over, never all three. Every trade has moved to perks, the Warder last, so both sides are asked to hold the same nodes (none) and channels and the same point arithmetic, every channel is still counted as read by something, nobody is left holding a node that is not a perk, and the walk through a tree waits for a trade on one.

title: Seven ways to fight, and a rite for each
why: Three melee, two ranged, a healer and one that fights with what fights beside it. Five new channels, every one of them a line that already decided its number — weapon_damage, hit_chance, hurt_player, wound_close, attack_of — plus hands and wind, which only wanted act_scope to call a swing by the thing in your hand rather than by `fighting`. And the rite, which is a node with an hour on it: same channels, same scope, same fold, so there is no second machinery for a number to disagree with itself in.

title: A fight on its own clock
why: A swing at the weapon's own pace and for its own wind, slower on tired arms; three stances; a struck beast that comes after you and lands its blows on its own clock; a bite that turns you only with the setting on and your feet still; a walk that leaves a fight; and a fight asked for mid-work that goes in hand at once. Every one asked of both sides off the same names.

title: A swing takes the seconds its weapon says
why: A short sword at fighting 1, 20, 47 and 70 swings every two seconds less skill, never under the floor, timed by `settle` as the browser times it and as the weapon's card says; armour counted by its family, a full set of leather and of plate each by what it counts for, in swing_burden itself and on the cards; a pack over what the back takes and a wagon driven leave it as it was; tired and wounded arms slow it the same on both sides; every weapon at its own pace; a fight asked for and a bite turned on timed the same; and every other job timed as it always was.

title: Heavy blows, hides and wounds
why: A kind that hits heavy draws back and lands it on you standing there, and falls short once you have stepped out of its reach; a cut, a puncture or a crush, and what each hide and each class of armour makes of it; a wounded arm that slows a swing; a maul that staggers, a knife that bleeds and never takes the last of it; and a blow from what you are not fighting landing harder. Both sides.

title: Packs, throwers and orders
why: One of a pack comes when another of its kind is on you, follows the first, and goes round to its own side of you; a thrower throws from where it stands and backs away when you close; a coward turns tail early and drags a hurt one of its kind with it, and a pack whose leader is gone runs; a companion that guards, attacks when told and falls back when told; and a bow drawn on the move. Both sides.

title: The safe ring round the spawn and the Runestones
why: Both sides measure the ring the same and keep the same kinds out of it; a roll of the wild and a stocked block inside it put out no monster, hunter or aggressive kind where outside they can; no hunt starts with either side in it, one of its own that comes in lets go and turns for home, and a fight the body started runs on.

title: Dodges, criticals, arrow heads, venom and threat
why: A blow on you is first rolled against your dodge, body control less the armour you wear; a blow or shot that lands can be critical, a knife's twice as often; a shot looses the arrows asked for, and a broadhead bleeds, a bodkin goes through a hide, a blunt staggers; a venomous bite drains until the wound is dressed and a burn wears armour faster; a creature turns on the companion that hurts it and back; and Examine weighs a fight up. Both sides.

title: A shield blocks
why: Each shield's chance, off its own share, its quality and the shields skill, the same on both sides; a blocked blow takes nothing, wears the shield by shield_wear and says so in the same words; the dodge is rolled first; and the card and the description say it.

title: A blow blocked or landed is marked on the body
why: Asked for: the blocking body plays a short block, and a body a blow lands on flinches, seen by the one struck and by every other player nearby. A blow blocked sets player.blocked_at to its instant with BLOCKED_SAID said and leaves hurt_at; a blow that lands, with a shield on or none, leaves blocked_at and sets hurt_at and hurt_where (a hit location, the one its line names: landedOf); a dodge or a ward taking it whole marks neither; the beat says them to the one struck (rpc_settle) and the roster reads them off the row.

title: A weapon reaches as far as its family
why: Every weapon's reach the same on both sides, a polearm a tile past a sword; a goblin out of a sword's reach refused in the same words and struck by a spear from the same spot; and the card and the help say it.

title: Patrons, faith spells and the spell bar
why: A patron is refused below its faith, taken at it and never twice; a spell is refused at a shut tier and from another patron, taken onto the bar, and closes its tier; the bar takes a spell only in a slot of its school; a call costs nothing when nothing is written behind it, its favour and its rest when it works, and is refused while it rests. Both sides, in the same words; and no door open but rpc_.

title: Meditation's tiers, Calm, and the Knowledge path
why: A path is chosen at twenty and kept by whoever chose before; a moved path's pick is refused in the browser's words and taken one a tier, a technique onto the bar's path slot. A sitting banks Calm off its place, up to favour's curve; a swirl near is worth more, a spot sat at since the woods turned half, and a blow ends it. Every Knowledge technique and discipline does what it says on both sides, and no path keeps a step. Seeded throughout.

title: The Love path on its tiers
why: Every one of Love's fifteen picks, on the island and in the browser: an old walker keeps the path and none of its steps; each technique costs its Calm, rests and does what it says (and one that finds nothing costs nothing); each discipline where its rule is -- a founder's ground, a tame, an age, a harvest, a fight, a knack, a breeding, a field in winter, the trees round a sitting. Seeded.

title: The Power path on its tiers
why: Every one of Power's fifteen picks, on the island and in the browser: wind, deep water, wounds, a walk and a load, a step up and a drop, a blow on chain, a heavy blow, a killing blow once an hour, hunger and thirst. Seeded.

title: The Blessing's spells
why: Every one of the fifteen pointed and cast as the door does it, and what it did read back: health, wounds, a hunt dropped, a boon kept, a zone on the ground, a tree a stage on. What lasts is asked of the rule it works through -- a blow, a body settling, a monster struck, a job timed, a taming, the beach, a hunter -- and one goes through rpc_cast_spell itself. Every number is the browser's own.

title: Justice's spells
why: Every one of the fifteen pointed and cast as the door does it: a mark through every blow, a Retribution owed and paid at the striker's settling, a Truce on both sides of a blow, a Summons a stranger's blow cannot take back, a Temper through any wear, an Oath split, a grave brought home, a Due Reward through skill_mult. Every number is the browser's own.

title: Chaos's spells
why: Every one of the fifteen pointed and cast as the door does it: a creature bleeding, running, cowering, struck or dead; health spent for favour or for power; a thing unmade. A Cower and Undying through hurt_player, a Pact through faith_arms, a Blood Feast through faith_feast, a Shroud through hunt_settle. None of them is cast on another person. Every number is the browser's own.

title: The Sworn Blade's spells and passives
why: The first fighting trade on spells and passives: twelve spells and six passives in six tiers that open on the trade's own level. Both sides hold the same rows; the level starts, learns and opens its tiers; a spell taken goes on the bar and is cast through the door for its stamina and its rest; every spell measured -- a blow at its share of a swing's, the same roll asked twice -- and every passive through the rule it changes, with the browser's numbers alike.

title: The Berserker's spells and passives
why: The second fighting trade on spells and passives. Both sides hold the same rows, what each spell wants in your hands included; every blow measured at its share of a swing's, the same roll asked twice; a hold, a bleed, a rage, an adrenaline, a whirlwind and an earthshaker on everything in reach and nothing past it; a spell refused without its axe, its maul or the health to pay; and every passive at the rule it changes, the browser's fold the island's.

title: The Pikeman's spells and passives
why: The third fighting trade on spells and passives. Both sides hold the same rows; every blow measured at its share of a swing's, the same roll asked twice; an Overreach as far past your reach as it says and no further; a creature slowed, warned off, dragged, pushed back by a blow or before its own, run through, and met at the edge of your reach; stamina back for everybody near; and every passive at the rule it changes, the browser's fold the island's.

title: The Archer's spells and passives
why: The fourth fighting trade on spells and passives. Both sides hold the same rows; every shot measured at its share of a draw's, the same roll asked twice, an arrow out of the pack for each; a Long Shot and a Point Blank as far or as near as they say and no further; a creature slowed, held, exposed to everybody's blows; a decoy struck instead of you; a next shot that cannot miss; a shot refused without a bow or arrows; and every passive at the rule it changes, the browser's fold the island's.

title: The Skirmisher's spells and passives
why: The fifth fighting trade on spells and passives. Both sides hold the same rows; every throw measured at its share of a swing's, the same roll asked twice; a Long Throw as far past your reach as it says and no further; two throws one after the other; a creature staggered, bled, glanced on from, and every one near it thrown at; a leap back; a quicker walk on the island's pace and in the answer the browser walks at; a creature marked for everybody's criticals; everything hunting you losing you; a throw refused without a javelin or a throwing axe; and every passive at the rule it changes, the browser's fold the island's.

title: The Chirurgeon's spells and passives
why: The sixth fighting trade on spells and passives. Both sides hold the same rows; every heal its share back on you or on somebody within its reach, and no further; every wound it closes closed by its share, the worst one or every one; a heal over time a second at a time; a dressing in a Surgeon's Hands twice as large, the same roll asked twice; a creature bled, one or all near you; a knife blow that gives back what it takes; a heal teaching the trade only in a fight; and every passive at the dressing it changes, the browser's fold the island's.

title: Quick Stitch closes the deepest wound
why: Reported: "quick stitch isn't working at all to lower wound severity". It closed the wound a dressing goes to first, scored bleeding and gone bad over depth, so once the deep one was dressed it took 30% of 3% off a light cut. Asked through the spell bar's door, on yourself and on somebody within reach: the deepest wound and only it goes to its share, the line names it with its depth before and after, the cost is spent and the spell rests, the next beat closes on from there, past reach and unhurt are refused with nothing spent; and the browser's wound window shows the depth the line says, the spell's text the island's.

title: A dressing goes past a wound gone bad
why: Reported: "Bandages don't seem to want to dress a wound if any of your wounds have gone bad." A dressing went on the worst wound, and a wound gone bad is always the worst, and nothing holds on one, so it was refused with a cut bleeding beside it. Both sides now pick the worst wound that has not gone bad, and are asked which wound that is, what it left the bad one as, what it said, and what the refusal says once the bad one is all there is.

title: A Healer's poultice heals twice and closes one more wound
why: Asked: "Healer's poultice -- first aid with a life mote heals x2 and closes one extra wound." The same body on both sides, every roll pinned: a dressing with a life mote heals twice what one without does and closes the next worst wound, never one gone bad, and uses the mote; one that slips keeps it; without a mote the entry is refused in the same words; on somebody beside you and on a wildermon the same; the entries' time and the life mote's text.

title: The Beastmaster's spells and passives
why: The seventh fighting trade on spells and passives. Both sides hold the same rows; every blow a spell has your companion strike its own blow at its share, the same roll asked twice, within its reach or as far as a Pounce leaps and no further; a creature put back, held or bled; every wild thing near it, or everything hunting you, turned on it; its health back; its blows larger and quicker while a spell holds; a creature that strikes you answered; a blow on either of you split between you; a wild creature tamed outright, into a crate when something follows you; its blows teaching the trade; and every passive at the rule it changes, the browser's fold the island's.

title: The Kindler's spells and passives
why: The eighth fighting trade on spells and passives, and the first of the arcane. Both sides hold the same rows; every spell wants a garnet or ruby focus in your pack and casts out of the best of them; fire at 100% an Ember out of it, to the last bit; every spell's fire at its share within its reach and no further; a burn its share of the creature's health a second, marking it burning; a Stoke waiting for the next fire; a Firebrand's longer burns; a Combust taking what a burn had left at once; a Blaze Aura burning a round at a time on the clock; a Meteor's splash and a Firestorm reaching every enemy within them; the fire teaching the trade and the school; and every passive at the rule it changes, the browser's fold and burn the island's.

title: The Binder's spells and passives
why: The ninth fighting trade on spells and passives, and the second of the arcane. Both sides hold the same rows; every spell wants a sapphire or diamond focus in your pack; a hold at 100% a Snare out of it and a shatter at 100% an Ember's force, to the last bit; a Bind and a Lock at their share, half on a monster, within their reach and no further, and a blow that turns a held creature on you not freeing it; a Shatter twice as large on one held; a Root taking no step where a creature tied to nothing walks on, and still striking; a Tether no further than its tether; Heavy Limbs, Dull Claws and Brittle at their shares, and the sentence after a shatter or a blow on a Brittle one saying what it is truly down to; a Snare out of the school counted a hold; Still Skin and Stillness on you; a Mire and a Mass Root on everything within their width; a Long Hold's longer holds and reach; and every passive at the rule it changes, the browser's fold the island's.

title: The Warder's spells and passives
why: The tenth and last fighting trade on spells and passives, and the third of the arcane. Both sides hold the same rows; every spell wants a topaz or emerald focus in your pack; a skin at 100% an Aegis's force out of it in hundredths of health, to the last bit, and the school's own Aegis laying one of its force in hundredths now; a Ward, Greater Ward and Deep Ward each over a smaller skin and none over a larger; a Ward Other within its reach and nobody beyond; a Sanctuary over everybody within its reach; a Thicken spent by the next skin; a Stoneskin and a Bastion of Stone at their shares; an Unbreakable letting no blow land; a Ward Burst's damage a hundredth of skin; a Ward Link's skin back, once; and every passive at the rule it changes -- Thick Skin, Protector, Overcharge, Second Wind, Thorns and Watchful -- the browser's fold the island's.

title: A cast says what it did
why: The browser drew an area spell on everything in its ring, a hold for its full seconds on a monster that is held for half of them, a flight on a monster a Fright is refused on, and a Stoke's glow for a minute after the fire spent it. Now the door's answer says who a cast reached and for how long, which it holds still, the waiting spells it spent and the skin it laid; and a Ward Link firing tells the Warder's browser. Through `rpc_cast_spell`, as a browser casts: a Firestorm, an Earthshaker, a Skull Crack on a monster and an animal, an Execute, a Fright and a Panic on both, a Stoke and a Thicken spent, a Ward Link fired.

title: Spell timers and the skin over you survive a reload
why: What spells leave on you is kept on your row and was only heard at the cast, so a reload emptied the effects row. A Thicken, a Ward Link and a Stoneskin cast for real and a skin laid by somebody else, read back off the join's row and off the beat, are listed by the effects row with their seconds left, the Thicken's multiplier and who laid the skin; nobody else's blessings and nothing run out ride along; and every key the island keeps a blessing under is one the row knows.

title: The single staircase, and wagons up wide ones
why: The second model of every flight, half the tile wide, up the half on your left or your right as you climb. Its bill in every material a flight is built in the same on both sides, and under the wide one's; planned with its hand, a wide one without, and a hand that is no hand taken as none; no hand on a ladder, and none let into the table on anything but a staircase; the hand in the ground read; walked up a storey as the wide one is, and taken out by its name. And wheels: a wagon up a wide staircase from its foot, through a doorway wide enough, off its head onto the floor and back down; not over its rails, up a single one or off the floor's edge; on the island standing on the storey it was driven to, its team kept in the traces up there and its reins not taken from below.

title: Down a staircase off its foot, with the storey over it floored
why: Off a flight across its foot is down to the storey under it, a floor over the foot or none; off its head or sides, the storey.

title: Mounts up wide staircases
why: "Mounts and carts can go up staircases, but not single staircases". Ridden up a wide staircase from its foot to storey 2 and along its floor, through doorways wide enough for wheels, and back down; not over its rails, up a single staircase or a ladder, or off the floor's edge. Replayed through rpc_move, never held back, the mount under its rider up there and its storey sent to everybody; no getting down or mounting a storey up, in the same words on both sides.

title: Nothing under a storey
why: A rider driving a wagon stored a storey up at a wide staircase's foot, with no floor there, is let down onto the ground on both sides (`Game.footing`, `storey_footing`), wagon, team and mount with it; a word up the flight pulled back to its pace onto the foot stays on the ground, and none down off it leaves storey 2 on the foot.

title: The outside staircase
why: "Allow building a staircase adjacent to a building to allow stairs going directly to the floor above from outside a building". A staircase, wide or single, on open ground just out past the footprint, its head against the building, up from the ground to storey 2. Every refusal in the same words on both sides; the same floor tile and bill planned; built, walked up from the ground, through a door off its head and down off its side; no part of the storey, its room or what a wall carries; taken out; and a jetty floor planned as before.

title: The spiral staircase
why: A tile a storey round a post, no climbing side: stepped onto and off at the storey walked on across any side, up and down it on its tile, stacked storey on storey down to a cellar. Planned inside, outside and down to a cellar with no side, refused and stacked in the same words on both sides, a single staircase's bill, built; walked up the stack and back down through rpc_move never held back, a change of storey with no spiral held back; mounts and wheels refused in the same words; a pinned storey's walk to it.

title: A settlement's workers eat from its own stores and carry the hod to its own work
why: An Ivarholm worker on Hildstead is not fed from Hildstead's crate, and is from Ivarholm's; planned work a tile past Ivarholm's edge, within its Brickling's reach, is not its work on either side.

title: A felling worker carries every log of the tree home
why: The tree of the most logs, felled by a Sapgnaw on both sides: the load is every log, and none is left at the stump.

title: Workers walk up a building's staircases to their work
why: A house of two storeys, a staircase up and a wall with a door across the upper storey: a worker with a load for a chest up there walks to the flight's foot, up it, through the door and back down; every leg a storey up on a floor and through no wall; a hod carrier fits a wall a storey up standing on that storey; a building with no staircase says "no stairs up to storey 2"; a floor taken from under one lets it down; and the browser draws it on its storey.

title: A worker stands at the foot of a flight a storey up, where the flight below comes off
why: Two flights in a line, the second's foot where the first comes off: the way to that tile a storey up is found and stops there, the way on up still climbs both, and a hod carrier fits a wall planned on that tile's side and never says no stairs up.

title: The help's search puts the sections with it in their heading first
why: "aqueduct" finds the Aqueducts section first, then the sections that only mention it, by how often; nothing for an empty search.

title: Recipes found off a goblin or an orc, read and used up, and the recipes they open
why: Cherry preserves and cottage pie shut until read, in the same words on both sides; a Recipe off a goblin's or an orc's carcass at the odds (the roll forced), one not read first; reading it opens the recipe and uses it up, and one already open is refused and kept; a simma cooks neither; and the beat says what is read.

title: An oven as a station, a ferment sealed and opened, and a dish served out to a group
why: A lit oven is the oven station and a brazier is not; a ferment seals a vessel ready in its time, refused too soon and opened for the result and the vessel back, one wanting a cellar refused above ground; a group's dish hands a share to each player in reach and the rest to the server. Fixtures only: no recipe uses them yet.

title: The Springlet, slow on land and a hare's pace in water, found only in deep water
why: Ridden on land half a walker's pace, flat; ridden in water a Thistlekit's pace in the same state, and the walk check holds a rider to each; it takes a rider into deep water; the wild puts it down in deep water only and its legs keep to it, at the rarest weight in the table; it eats fish and needs a saddle and a bridle.

title: A mount under you walks as you walk, and a team in the traces with its cart
why: A saddled Thistlekit ridden across open ground with the wildlife the island's: going, facing your way and its gait stepping every frame, under you, and stopped when you stop. And two in the traces of a large cart, driven by you and by somebody else: going every frame, the way the cart goes, ahead of it.

title: The path search finds the same paths remembering what it asked of each tile
why: The search as it was and as it is, from the same starts to the same goals on three rough islands: within a click and far past the square remembered, by the edge, near, partial and cut short. The same path, tile and storey, and the same verdict, every time.

title: A bridge up a storey is walked across and under, every lane, on both sides
why: A marble bridge three lanes wide, both ends on storey 4: every lane holds a body at storey 4 and nobody at storey 3, a walk along each lane stays on storey 4 (`rpc_move`), a walk on the ground under it is drawn under it, and a pinned storey's click on the deck ends on it.

title: Under a bridge on foot, mounted, in a cart and in a wagon, on both sides
why: One lane of marble, a rope bridge and three lanes of marble at storey 4, each over a sunken road: on foot, mounted, in a large cart and in a wagon, a walk down the road is found and walked under the deck on the ground, drawn under it (`driveRule`, `pieceOnDeck`), and every word to `rpc_move` along it is let through (`walk_share`). Across the decks as before: a cart over marble, not over rope; a wagon over neither.

title: A bridge between two buildings' storey 4 is crossed at storey 4, and its end's wall planned
why: Two buildings five storeys high, wide staircases up to storey 4 and a marble bridge three lanes wide between their storey-4 floors: on foot and mounted, storey 4 pinned, a walk from one floor to the other crosses the deck at storey 4 every step (`stepRule`, `rideRule`; was down the staircases and back up, mounted), every word of it answered at storey 4 by `rpc_move`; a worker's way (`creature_way`) crosses it too; and the wall on a lane's end border, picked from the deck's side (`wallAcross`), is planned on both sides in the same words.

title: Storey mode
why: "Navigating and building 2nd+ storey is super clumsy. We have a storey toggle UI, lets lean into that. Clicking that toggle hides all other storey, allowing players to move onto and along that storey and build options exclusively for that storey". Pinned on storey 2 of a hall with a staircase, a jetty and an outside staircase: a click answers on its floor, the jetty, the outside staircase's head and the open air beside it, at the floor's height, and not on far ground; a walk there ends on storey 2 up the staircase, and replayed through rpc_move is never held back; the jetty's and the footprint's rows name storey 2. Drawn in Chrome: no ground-floor wall or piece pinned on storey 2, a click on its floor picks it with storey 2's menu and none of the ground's jobs; Auto as before.

title: No plan on a bare side of storey 2 and up
why: "On storey 2+ you can select a wall option 'no plan' that removes the plan model and leaves the wall blank". A bare outside side of storey 2 marked No plan and marked out again, in the same words on both sides; refused on the ground storey, inside, off the building, where a wall is planned and twice; a wall planned on it, the storey removed or the building removed clears it; a fresh browser is handed it by the ground read; with every side marked the storey is as open as before (level_gap, a roof refused). Drawn in Chrome: no plan model on a marked side, one on every other; No plan and Mark out on storey 2's menu only.

title: Plans over an area, their totals, the last plan undone, and a roof as its own storey
why: "Previews for multi-tile plans, cost totals before you commit, undo for a misplaced plan, and extend the storey mode to roofs". Walls all round, a whole roof and a footprint's rectangle planned in one call (rpc_plan_area), each piece by its own refusal and performer, said once; refused whole out of reach, a refused piece left out and counted, a bad list refused; the totals one bill times the pieces; the last plan, an area's or a single click's, undone by Remove wall, Remove floor and Remove from plan (rpc_plan_undo), not past its time. Drawn in Chrome at desktop and phone width: the ghost, the bar inside the screen, Plan and Undo; pinned on a roof, the roof's menu only, a pitched roof picked on its slope and not walked onto.

title: Glassblowing, glass panels, bottles and the stained glass wall
why: The Artisan's fourth trade, at a hot smelter: sand melted into lumps, a lump blown into the panel every window, bay and glasshouse roof is glazed with, a bottle, and a gem and sand fired into the panes a stained glass wall is leaded from. Each job the same on both sides and made on the island; a failed firing keeps its gem; the stained glass wall's bill, and a bottle's room, alike on both sides.

title: A stone, and what you can get out of it
why: The arcane, which has no mana in it. A focus is a cut gem in a silver claw and every number the system needs was already on the item: the kind, the cut, the find, and how much is left. A stone worn through crumbles down the same path that takes a rotten haunch off the ground. This asks both sides for the three schools and six spells, compares the four pieces of arithmetic fed the same inputs, and lands all three effects — a burn, a hold and a skin — including that a skin spent against a blow stays spent.

title: What is lying about, going off where it lies
why: ground_sweep rewrote every thing on an island's ground once a second — 95 microseconds a row, whether anything had changed or not, which was the whole of a world round on a busy island. It is charged in steps now, and the claim that makes that safe is that the elapsed terms telescope: two hours then one is three hours. That is asked here to the last bit, along with the cap, the order, and — in buffers rather than milliseconds, so it means the same on a slow runner — that a quiet round does not read the ground.

title: The island saying that it cannot save
why: On 09-25 the database filled and went read-only, and a refused action did nothing on the screen at all. The banner comes on at the first door refused with 25006, stays through doors that only read, and goes when a refused door answers again.

title: Islands that go
why: Seven islands the live test founded between 09-17 and 09-20 were still on the project, and islands nobody played were kept a month. Now the test's island lasts a day, a founding that never opened goes after a day, an island nobody came ashore on after a week, the home island never -- and their letters and bridge spans go too.

title: A cheaper stir
why: The stir was 94% of a round on the live island: every round walked whatever was heading within 104 tiles of a body, against the 40 a browser is shown. Now a wild creature ten tiles off is walked every round and one seventy tiles off stands until somebody comes near; the tame there are still settled, every ten seconds.

title: A cheaper stir, the same island
why: The search for a worker's next tile, its stores, its stations, its meals and a recipe its stores hold do less for the same answer, and a round settles each creature once. One island, run as it is and with the stir as it was (stirload-before.sql), from the same moment and seed: a round of the clock and an hour of nine workers' day leave it the same, creature for creature and item for item.

title: A creature's numbers planned once, a settle writing what changed
why: A creature's numbers and its stores' room are planned once a session, not once a settle; a worker's or companion's settle writes its row only when it changed; a step writes no index. Each function put back as the SQL it was: every number for every kind, stage, trait, gear and channel and every piece of furniture the same to the last bit, a round of the clock and an hour of work the same island, with fewer creature rows written and none that changed left unwritten.

title: A queue put in order
why: Asked for: the jobs queued listed in the crafting window, dragged into another order and taken out with a cross. The jobs waiting go into the order asked and the job in hand stays in hand; a job left out is put out of mind and said so; a list that changed since it was seen, or an order that is not one, is refused and nothing moves; a job put down by a walk moves like any other. Both sides, in the same words.

title: Goods that change hands
why: The stalls had never sold anything: a price and a mailbox were looked up by a kind no builder leaves. This builds the pieces the way a builder does and goes through the doors: priced, read off the board at a mailbox, bought at the counter, not taken off somebody else's stall; and a wildermon in its crate offered, posted, laid on a stall and bought, and kept by whoever ends up with the crate.

title: Finding things on the market
why: "The stalls work, but finding things in them doesn't." Through the doors on Hoarding: a sale off a stall and one brought to an order written down with the quality of what went; rpc_prices with a day's average quality; rpc_sales, a thing's last sales newest first and no more than sales_shown(); away from the board, the nearest settlement token. Drawn in Chrome: Find across every stall, by the price of one, by QL and by distance, each against the month's average; Walk, Pin once, Buy at the counter; History and Order; the last board read still found in away from the token; the map handed every stall; nothing off the side of a phone.

title: A shop counter, on both sides
why: Asked for: a wall with a counter in it, the shop's goods on the inside and its customers in the street. Planned only in a ground floor wall with open ground beyond it; nobody walks through it and it hides nothing; its keeper sets goods out on it and prices them as on a stall; a buyer buys from the street side and within reach only, refused in the same words on both sides; the till and the takings, the board at a mailbox, a creature crate on it, the wall not taken out while there are goods or takings in it, and its store opened the same when a hod worker lays its last piece.

title: A lantern post, on both sides
why: Asked for: a timber post with a lantern on an iron arm and a stone pillar with one in its top, each taking a fitted lantern and its candles as a carried lantern does. Fitted, candled, lit, burned down, put out and taken down with the same refusals, sentences and numbers on both sides; the candle the same length at every quality; at night a light of the lantern's reach, where it hangs, that the ground round it is seen by from far off; a padlock that keeps the lantern for the key; and no post set down with its arm into a wall, nor a wall planned or raised across a post's arm.

title: While you were away
why: The island counts, for somebody who has gone, the loads their workers put away, the young born to their wildermon, what their stalls sell and the parcels posted to them, and hands the counts over on the way back in. Driven through the real sale, parcel, birth and worker paths, with a sale made while the owner is there not counted, and the browser's lines made of the island's answer.

title: Island leaderboards
why: Top skills, best-bred wildermon and biggest settlements, from one door. An island of three is ranked place by place: wild ones left out, no trait named anywhere in the answer, somebody off the island refused, and the window's lines held to the numbers the island ranks by.

title: Bred records, per kind, the best ever bred
why: Each base stat at birth and the trait total, with the young one's name, breeder and day, written at a birth only where it beats what stands, kept when it dies or is let go, and read back the same through rpc_bred_records and the boards, on both sides.

title: A young one knows its dam, its sire and where each trait came from
why: "A pedigree on the creature window. Show the dam, the sire and which traits came from which, so breeding can be planned." Both sides breed the same pair five hundred times and are asked that every young one names its dam and sire, that each trait says the dam, the sire, both, a fresh roll or bred up in the same five words and only where that is true, and that a covering from before has no pedigree. The browser's goes through a save; the island sends somebody else's only as far as they can read the traits. And a line: each young one's depth on each channel is one past the deeper of its parents' where it carries a trait there, six generations down one line stop at the cap, what a line is worth is the same in both sides' blood, and nothing already on an island stands past one.

title: A pairing says what it would throw before it is made
why: "Before a pairing is confirmed, show for that pair: each trait either parent carries, with the chance the foal inherits it; the chance the foal comes out at each tier better than common; the chance of a mutation and its tier; the pedigree bonus the foal would start with." The odds are worked out exactly from the covering's rule, add up, land where a hundred thousand draws, the birth and the island's breed_traits land, are said as closely as the breeder's husbandry reads, and the island rolls a wild trait by the browser's one rule.

title: One young in two hundred is born with a mutation
why: A trait neither parent carries, a tier above the best of theirs, in the young one's lowest-tier slot, said at the birth. Both sides, with the rolls forced either side of the odds.

title: A wild one now and then comes in a pale or dark form, or large or small
why: A colour form at one wild spawn in five hundred, a fifth palette per kind, and a size form at one in two hundred, large or small, each off its own roll and never a monster. Both sides roll it the same way and over a large seeded draw as often as it says; the stocking puts them out through it; a large one's health and a small one's speed are its blood; taming keeps them; a young one has each at a quarter for each parent with it; the field guide marks each form seen and tamed; the island sends them and the browser draws them.

title: Every ogre is a Menhir, Gatebreaker or Barrowback Ogre, the same on both sides
why: Three subspecies, one for each of the ogre's variants: the island puts them out evenly among its three and sends the variant; the browser names, states and draws each by its own, with the same health and blow. Both agree for a set of ids the island sends.

title: Every dragon is a Runewing Dragon, Runestone Drake or Stormcoil Dragon, the same on both sides
why: Three subspecies, one for each of the dragon's variants, by the ogre's mechanism: the island puts them out evenly among its three and sends the variant, and no dragon is left in the fourth there was; the browser names, states and draws each by its own, with the same health and blow. Both agree for a set of ids the island sends.

title: Every orc is a Runebrand, Ironshield or War-chanter Orc, the same on both sides
why: Three subspecies, one for each of the orc's variants: the island puts them out evenly among its three and sends the variant; the browser names, states and draws each by its own, with the same health and blow. Both agree for a set of ids the island sends.

title: Every goblin is a Scrapper, Raider or Hexer Goblin, the same on both sides
why: Three subspecies, one for each of the goblin's variants: the island puts them out evenly among its three and sends the variant; the browser names, states and draws each by its own, with the same health and blow. Both agree for a set of ids the island sends.

title: Live updates over Broadcast
why: The island sends land, lines and packs itself, once a statement, with realtime.send (kept locally by the shim), and no longer through Postgres Changes. On Bigness with one body not away: a tile under him goes to his block and one beside it, one far off goes nowhere, a hundred and fifty in one statement are one message; his lines and pack go to his own topic, nobody away is sent anything; and who may listen to which topic, through the policy as well.

title: Everything on a rack in one list, taken across its crates
why: Asked for off a rack of eight rows all reading "Seeds": "is it possible to just condense the inventory instead of having to go through each box?" Open all piles the rows of every crate on a rack as the pack would (`stack_key`), and a count taken from a line comes out of its crates in the rack's order, one take_from_store a row, passing over a crate shut to you. Both sides, over the same rack, the same rows and the same plan.

title: A caravel, and the people she carries
why: Her bill against the sailing boat's, her hold and her three places, on both sides; then in a harbour cut for it, a passenger comes aboard, goes where she goes, is not in the water and steps ashore only with land in reach; the fourth is told she is full; a helm somebody present holds is theirs and one left by somebody gone away is taken from her deck; she is not picked up with anybody aboard; and the island says who is aboard her, in the browser's words.

title: What goes wrong in a browser is written down on the island
Buy orders on the board
why: What somebody wants, with the whole price held against it, filled out of anybody else's pack and sent by the post. Through the doors on Hoarding: put up only at a token or a mailbox and only with the coins, change and all; listed with who and where; not filled by its owner, past what it wants, or with the wrong kind or quality, a stack put by, a pick in the hand or a bag with a rope in it; the poorest that will do first, paid there and then, counted for an owner who is away; taken back, or lapsed after a week, for what it still holds; and two people filling it at once, one after the other.

title: A field guide of the wildermon
why: A page for every kind, marking whether you have seen, tamed and bred it, and where it lives. Each page's lines are its kind's own rules read out, number for number, and nothing is said without its rule. Both sides mark a kind seen when one stands in view out of a crate, tamed when an offering takes or a catch comes out of a trap, and bred when a young one is born to a dam somebody keeps; the browser keeps its book in the save, and the island takes a sighting only while one of the kind is standing near you, answers a second one as had, refuses too many at once and anybody not on the island, and hands the book back whole to its owner and to nobody else.

title: One purse, two payments at once
why: Two payments out of one purse at the same moment: the first pays, the second waits for it, counts what is left and is refused.

title: One of every tool to come ashore with, kept through a death
why: The kit is one of every tool the island asks for, QL 20, issued, the browser's list; coming ashore gives it and the stake; issued cannot be improved; a death leaves it on the body; a missing piece is given again on coming ashore, once; a player cannot call the top-up; a Starter tool is refused on a barter side, in a deal, on a stall price and for an order, in the browser's words.

title: Every third tree rollover, the wild reset
why: The island resets every as many rollovers as the browser says; a reset takes every wild one that can turn over and leaves a tamed one, one in a fight and a monster; every region is owed its stocking; an island is owed its reset with its woods done and that many rollovers on; tree_tick resets an owed island; a player cannot call any of it.

title: A grave where you fell
why: On both sides, on dry ground with deep water off it: a death buries the pack, the hands, the toolbelt and every bag with what is in it where the body fell, and says so with the hour put in from the rule; what is worn stays on, and so do a crate with a wildermon in it and what is held in a deal; in deep water the grave is on the nearest dry ground in reach; a second death digs beside the first and one carrying nothing digs none; only its owner opens it or takes from it, anybody else is told whose it is and shown nothing in it, and nobody takes a spadeful out of it; its hour up the sweep takes it off an index of when graves crumble, and it is marked on its owner's map and survives a save.

title: An island's keepers, and the four things only they may do
why: Who keeps an island: whoever founded it, and anybody the deploy's own SQL (supabase/owner.sql, run here against a test address) made an owner of every island. Every owner door refuses everybody else, and before it does anything at all. Then each tool does what it says: who is on, a body moved off a stuck spot and told who moved it, a mute that refuses talk, letters and a parcel's note and lifts on time or when lifted, a pile cleared, and the trail of all of it.

title: A keeper kicks and bars, and anybody reports
why: Only keepers kick, unbar, read the open reports and mark them handled. A kick logs the body off as the idle log-out does and sends its browser `kicked`; a barred body is refused by move, act, say, a letter and coming back ashore, on that island only, until a keeper lifts the bar or its time is up. Reports: a reason from the list, a note cut to the most kept, one about the same body and five in all a day, the one reported never told, and what is past keeping deleted. Prints what rpc_move costs with nobody barred.

title: What everybody on an island has on
why: A body is drawn in its gear, and somebody else's pack is not yours to read: the island says what each body has on, a slot at a time, as the thing, how rare, what it is made of and its dye -- and not a thing put down but still written as worn, nor anything of its quality; to somebody on the island, and to nobody else.

title: Climbing that stays climbed
why: Reported: "climbing seems to level up then resets to 1". The browser raised it for itself and the island never did, so the book the island sends wrote it back. The same hillside goes to both sides: the island pays a go a step off the walk it is told about, at the browser's rate; the browser pays nothing where the island owns the body and the same goes where it does not; and flat ground, a gentle slope, a storey and a saddle teach nothing on either.

title: Driving and sailing
why: Two skills of the reins and the helm: each makes what it steers go faster by the same sum on both sides, the island lets the faster pace stand, and each is paid a go for every tile the cart or the hull goes into under way -- and nothing for a cart nothing pulls.

title: Mote swirls turn over with the woods, and Elementalism collects them
why: Every dawn the day's swirls go and five hundred new ones are put down: water on water, and on land the island of the chart's own element, or dark or light one time in a hundred each -- the same chart and the same rule in a game of your own. A collect gives one mote under Elementalism 20 and five from 80, trains it, and takes the swirl for everybody; the second of two at one swirl is told it is gone. Every roll is seeded.

title: Dye is boiled red, yellow or blue and mixed by pouring, the same on both sides
why: A boil of each dyestuff leaves a bucket of its one primary; dye poured into dye mixes by the litres of each, and goes in with nothing else; its QL is its brightness, black at 1 and white at 100; a thing dyed takes exactly the dye's hex. The hex, the colour word, a pour and Examine's words are held against the browser over thousands of seeded mixes, and a pot, a dyed tunic and a dyed banner from before come out as the browser's save loader makes them.

title: A dye is written down on papyrus and boiled again at its QL and not higher, the same on both sides
why: Make a recipe on a bucket or a barrel of dye takes one sheet of papyrus and records the dye's parts and QL; its name and Examine say the colour, the hex and, per bucket of lye, the kilos of each primary's dyestuff, held against the browser over hundreds of seeded mixes. Boil from recipe gives exactly the recipe's parts at the boil's QL capped at the recipe's, takes each share and the lye, keeps the recipe, halves the weight for a Double Boil and damages the dyestuffs and the lye by their QL on a failed boil. Every refusal in the same words.

title: Dye is scrubbed off with a brush, the same on both sides
why: Scrub off dye on a dyed cloth in the pack and a dyed banner set down, Scrub off paint on a painted side, Scrub off floor paint on a painted floor: each refused without a brush in the general tool words, with nothing to remove, padlocked against you or out of reach in the same words on both sides; a go of each comes out plain, says the lye removals' words, wears the brush a go's worth once and uses no lye.

title: A failed craft damages what it would have used, by its QL, the same on both sides
why: The damage at QL 0 to 100; only the units a go would have used, the pile's damage up by that over its count; units taken to the most there is gone; a litre input losing that share of its litres; a smelting and a cooking recipe that used to lose everything damaging instead and handing nothing back; Nothing Wasted, Keep the Stone and Second Heat sparing it; the anvil's casting and lump, and a brew's ingredients and water. Every line in the same words.

title: Five Runestones stand on the shore, and a Telestone takes you to them
why: The stones stand on the shore of the island's inner bay, on its generated ground, laid over a test's smaller world by scale, and their nine tiles refuse every job that changes the ground or puts something on it; nothing walks into one. What was made on those tiles before is taken back, the ground put back to the generated ground, and whoever stood there is put beside the stone. A Telestone is cut from five earth motes and a stone brick and reaches 300 tiles and makes you wait a day at QL 1, 5000 tiles and an hour at QL 100, on a straight line between; the wait is the traveller's. Every refusal, the landing tile and the words, on both sides; a word about walking from before a journey does not pull the body back. Every roll is seeded.

title: A first join picks a Runestone and starts 2 tiles from it
why: "new players should select between the 5 runestones for spawning, and spawn 2 tiles away from that stone on selection". A newcomer naming each stone starts on the first free tile of the ring 2 tiles out from its edge, the browser's ring in the browser's order, on a tile a body stands on; that ring built on, the next ring out. A stone that is not one is refused at the door; somebody already on the island stays where they were; no stone, or a test's world, is the spawn. Drawn in Chrome: the five on the boot card, by name and where each stands, for a first join only.

title: On death, wake at a Runestone or a settlement of yours
why: "show that screen on death, with an indicator of how far each rune is from your corpse, or an option to respawn at your deed token or one you belong to". A death is as it was (the spawn, whole, a grave where the body fell); the beat then offers where it fell and its own and member settlements. Each stone wakes it on a first join's ring; a settlement next to its token, the next tile when that one is built on; a stranger's settlement, a body that never died or stepped off the spawn, and a pick that is none of these are refused; stay, or never picking, is the spawn. Drawn in Chrome over the world: the five and the two settlements with their distances and pictures, keys kept in it, a refusal shown again with why.

title: A death in a new character's first 24 h played takes nothing
why: "a grace period after death for new players -- no penalty for dying during a character's first 24 hours of playtime (time actually played, not time since sign-up)". Under the grace a death digs no grave and lowers nothing, and says the grace left in the browser's words; at it and past it, a grave and a death's bars as before. Played time counts the stretch body_settle settles while in the game, and nothing away, unheard or after a gap; the beat says the grace left, and the effects row shows it.

title: Sleep logs you off in a bed, and the sleep bonus, the same on both sides
why: Beds that log the player off and begin the stage of sleep bonus gain while the player is offline. Sleep at any hour in a bed of yours or on a settlement of yours; refused on a stranger's, with a job going, in a fight and mounted. Done through rpc_act: logged off, asleep, the beat says so and nothing is asked of it. The next join wakes it beside the bed (on a free tile round it when that ground is gone, where the bed stood when the bed is), with the time asleep at the bed's rate, capped, said. Switched on: skill gain doubled, a minute drained a minute; off: kept. The words and numbers against sleep.ts.

title: Enchanting, the paper press and three melee enchantments, the same on both sides
why: Papyrus is pressed at a paper press, built with carpentry and set down, and refused without one. A scroll is written from papyrus and two motes with enchanting -- Firebrand from fire (a burn), Razoredge from ice (a knife's bleed), Concussion from earth (a stun) -- never better than its sheet; one that fails loses its motes and damages the sheet, or uses it up. Enchant puts one into a melee weapon at the average of enchanting and the scroll's QL as a percent, from 5% to 95%, held to the scroll's QL and the weapon's own; otherwise 30 damage, or 5% of the time the weapon gone. Every refusal, the name's marker, Examine, the post, a counter and a save; each enchantment just under and just over its chance on a hit, through a swing; and the stun itself: nothing moves or strikes for its two seconds, and a second stun starts again rather than adding on. Every roll is set.

title: Enchanting, part two
why: The enchantments after the first three, on both sides: each scroll's motes (Leeching's a life and a dark), what Examine says each does at its quality, the refusal that names what it goes on, and what each does, measured the same way: Venomfang's venom just under and just over its chance, a Gale's swing, a Nightblade's critical chance, a Sunstrike on a goblin and on a cartling, a Leeching's health back on every hit with no roll, and how far a Tidecaller puts a blow back; a Farsight bow's reach, and a Flamearrow's burn and a Frostbite's slow on a shot that lands, the slow in the creatures' door too; and what is worn: Stoneskin and Emberward to their caps, Featherstep's walk, Bulwark's block, Shadowcloak by night, and Thornhide's payback.

title: Enchanting, part three
why: The enchantments on new kinds of thing, on both sides: the scrolls, Examine's words, the refusals by kind, and what each does -- the jewel slot's Scholar's Band, Knackstone, Steady Heart, Hearthbound, Favoured and Stillwater.

title: The enchanter's plinth, the same on both sides
why: Enchant, putting a scroll into a thing, is done standing at an enchanter's plinth and nowhere else, as papyrus is pressed at a paper press. Built with masonry and a trowel from 32 stone bricks, 12 mortar, 2 stone slabs, a light mote and a dark mote, refused a mote short; set down as any piece; Enchant refused away from one in the station rule's words, taken 2.3 tiles from its middle and refused at 2.5 (the station reach, 2.4); a scroll still written away from one. In the browser, the plinth in use while you or anybody else enchants within that reach, and the light it throws.

title: A rune lantern post, on both sides
why: Asked for: a squat carved stone pillar with a band of runes round it, built with masonry from stone bricks and light motes and set down like other furniture, that lights like a lantern of its QL and never needs fuel. The same recipe, item, words and moss on both sides; refused short of a mote in the same words, then built; set down, kept out of a cellar, picked up, and none of a lantern post's jobs applying to it; what a ground read sends of it; and at night a lantern's reach at its quality from the middle of the pillar, the ground round it in sight from far off, still alight hours on.

title: An altar goes up on your own ground
why: Asked for: "Make the altar only craftable within deed perimeter". The same recipes carry the flag on both sides, and both refuse an altar in the same words off a settlement of yours: on one you founded it goes up, to its last tile and not a tile past it; on a neighbour's it does not, until you are a citizen of it.

title: Baubles, found, restored and set into the altar
why: Asked for: a share of archaeology's finds are baubles, restored like relics and set into a settlement's altar for bonuses to its citizens on its land. Both sides hold the same tiers, skills and words, read each other's baubles, refuse a setting in the same words, and give the same time, skill and yield -- through the clock, on the island.

title: Dirt is collected, moss cut, and moss and grass planted on dirt, the same on both sides
why: Asked for: collect dirt on its tile, as clay and sand are collected; moss cut off a moss tile as grass is cut, giving moss; and ten moss planted on a dirt tile to turn it to moss. Both sides offer and refuse the same, give dirt off dirt and moss off moss (digging moss still gives dirt), keep a cut tile short until it grows back, and turn the dirt to moss for the same moss. And a tile of dirt dug bare still shows the rock on both sides, where a bed of sand stays sand: dirt is collected from, but it is not a bed. Then, after a player found no way to plant grass: as much mixed grass as moss planted on dirt turns it to grass, refused in the same words.

title: A find nobody has restored takes no repair
why: Asked for: an artifact that has not been restored cannot be repaired, and one that breaks before it is restored is gone. Repair, a repair kit and Mend refuse a fragment or a tarnished bauble in the same words on both sides, a worker mending the stores passes it by, Restore takes it at any damage short of breaking, and at the most damage a thing takes it is gone.

title: A sacrifice at the altar, and the souls it leaves
why: Asked for: rare, supreme and fantastic things given up at the altar fill every nutrient; one in a hundred leaves a soul of the same rarity, which gives an ordinary thing that rarity. Both sides refuse the same things in the same words and do the same.

title: The dragon keeps to Volcano Isle, and wildermon go by their kinds' names
why: Asked about: a dragon stood up on the Crescent, and tamed wildermon were still called Rabba and the like. The dragon stands up on Volcano Isle alone, a grand map's hoard (a dragon guards it) is buried there, no wildermon keeps its kind's old name, on both sides and in a save, and a save's wild dragon off Volcano Isle is gone, as the island's went.

title: Each island's own fruit trees, carried onto an island founded before them
why: Reported: with the fog off the map drew lemons on Volcano Isle, and walking there found none. The live island's land is from 15 September and the fruit trees were held to their islands on the 18th; the move tool's fruit move (tools/move-ground.ts `fruitHome`) grows them there. Lemons on Volcano Isle only, ages kept, a tile in tile_change and a planted oak left alone, written down once, a second run a no-op.

title: Each island's own fruit trees, by kind, on woods that have turned over
why: The fruit move by tile found 28 trees on the live island: a tree lives six days and seeds its own kind round it, so after fifty days nothing stands where founding day put it. The move by kind (tools/move-ground.ts `fruitByKind`) takes the apples and olives as they stand: OWN_FRUIT_SHARE of them off settlements become the island's own fruit at their own age, lemons on Volcano Isle only, nothing else changed, written down once, a second run a no-op.

title: With the fog off, the map and the world show the island and not the seed
why: The same report: the fog-off map drew every square from the seed, read from the island or not. A square not read is unseen with the fog off and asked for once; the asks are read a LAND_STEP square at a time, nearest the body first, LAND_UNFOGGED_EVERY apart, and each is drawn afresh; read, it shows the island's tree, not the seed's.

title: A hod carrier brings a wall what the stores hold
why: Asked about: a level 1 cobbe did not bring marble brick and mortar to a planned marble wall seven tiles off. It now takes the nearest wall wanting something its keeper's stores hold, crates and furniture alike, what is furthest behind the bill first, on both sides.

title: A worker off its ground walks back to it
why: Reported: a Tinka sent home from 300 tiles away did not move and could not be selected. A worker past its ground walks back first, a short leg at a time so that whoever is near it is told of it, and an errand trade with nothing to run wanders in round the token.

title: A wildermon works round its keeper, into storage in reach
why: Asked for: "Allow wildermon to Work Around Me, provided there is storage nearby (carts and wagons and accessible boats included)." Its ground is its keeper's tile; its loads go into crates, furniture, carts, wagons and boats its keeper may use within its range; none, or full, and it idles and drops nothing. Stop, or its keeper offline, and it goes back into its crate or to following, on both sides.

title: A settlement's stores are read off the settlement
why: The world clock timed out every round inside a hod carrier's choice of wall: every piece of furniture on the island was reckoned, once a wall. The stores read are exactly the keeper's, and fast with three thousand stocked chests elsewhere on the island.

title: Restored relics are used on a wildermon
why: Asked for: a restored bone comb takes a stage off a wildermon's age, an old file makes it a step rarer one time in twenty, an old pot puts a point into one of its base stats, ten at most a stat, and its card says its stats. Each restores into an ancient thing of its own, is used up, and is refused and kept where it would do nothing. The same on both sides, and the island sends your own one's points.

title: An ancient lamp rekindles a trait
why: Asked for: the old lamp restores into an ancient lamp, which used on a wildermon of yours rerolls its lowest-tier trait at that tier or better, one time in twenty a tier higher, at the top tier among the top tier, never a trait it carries, and is used up. The same on both sides, with the rolls forced and sampled; an old lamp held is an ancient lamp in a save and on the island.

title: Tracking reads the way to the nearest wild one
why: Asked for: a tracking skill, and a Track button in the field guide that points to the nearest wild one of a kind you have seen, more finely the higher your Tracking. Refused for a kind not seen and a monster; the nearest wild one found past kept ones and other kinds, none past the reach; the reach, spread, bands, reading and line the same on both sides; each band exact with the roll forced; a go trains Tracking; through rpc_act and the clock, arrow and all.

title: Rare ingredients make rare work more likely
why: Asked for: a rare+ ingredient raises the chance a craft comes out that rare by its share of the ingredients: two, one supreme, is +50% supreme. The same chance of each step and the same words on both sides; many goes of mortar off a supreme clay come out supreme about half the time on both, and plain clay as ever; a full bucket is no ingredient; a rare lump or casting at the anvil is all of it.

title: A stack dropped on a crate rack fills its crates one by one
why: Asked for: "Allow dragging inventory to a Crate shelf, where the crates on it will fill one by one according to available space." A rack holds nothing itself, so a drop on one went nowhere. Three crates of different room and one that is not yours: a stack bigger than the first crate's room runs on into the next ones in the rack's order and passes the other over, a stack bigger than all of it leaves the rest in the pack, and both sides say it in one line and refuse in the same words.

title: A settlement's places count its own workers
why: Reported: two wildermon at work and a third refused as the fifth of five. The browser counted a neighbour's workers within sight against your settlement's places; only your own count now.

title: A hod carrier works on everything built off a bill
why: Asked for: the Brickling works on floors and the rest of a deed's building, not only ground-floor walls. Walls on any storey, floors, roofs, stairs, ladders, columns, bridge and aqueduct spans and foundations, chosen and fitted piece for piece the same on both sides, and an hour of one at work on each.

title: A hod carrier says what it wants and puts back what nothing wants
why: Seen on the island: hod carriers idle with "nothing in range" while work in range wanted marble brick and glass the stores did not hold, one holding mortar nothing wanted. Now `stock`, naming what is wanted, the same words on both sides; `range` only with no work at all; and the unwanted piece back in the stores.

title: A worker far from anybody still walks home
why: Reported: a Tinka sent home from far away stood where its keeper left it, out of reach of the sweeps round the players. The clock walks every worker off its ground whoever is near.

title: Every awake player gets a share of the round
why: Reported: "Mortarbacks still not working when I log in", their card saying nobody awake was near. One player's country full of wildlife coming due spent the whole of every round. A keeper's own wildermon first on a budget of their own (`kept_sweep`), each awake tile a fair share of the rest in a different order each round, tame before wild.

title: A worker says why it is idle
why: Asked: a worker on a settlement often stands idle and nothing says why. Each cause is kept as a code and a number and said on its card in the same words on both sides: no barrel with room for water, no reed bed in its range, nothing in the stores, walking home, and on the island a keeper away or nobody near enough for the clock.

title: A worker keeps a ledger of the last island day
why: Asked: per deed worker, what it did over the last island day, in two buckets keyed by the island day so it stays bounded. Counted where the work is, rolled over at the day boundary, the same on both sides.

title: A wildermon keeps its lifetime at work
why: Off the day's ledger as it is written: what it handled by the thing, its cycles and skill, its best island day, and its time working, idle by the reason and resting, kept by the row write that writes the ledger. The same on both sides, across days, sent to its keeper only, said on its card, and what it costs a worker's step measured.

title: A magga sorts the bins
why: Asked: the Magga "now also sorts raw material bins and craft material bins". With nothing lying about it takes a stack out of a settlement store into the bin that takes it and has room, never out of a bin or a padlocked or marked store, and says why when idle.

title: A wild thing goes after its span and the stretch is stocked afresh
why: Asked: "I havent seen a single one of the new 60 wildermon." Country was put out once and only topped up for what was killed, so 52 new kinds had no wild head at all. A wild one with nothing to do with anybody now goes at its stretch's stocking once it is a day to two old, by its id, the same on both sides; a young one, a tamed one, one fighting or fought, trapped, marked, coaxed or acted on, and a monster stay; the one-off sweep takes every such one whatever its age; and stocked over and over a stretch shows every kind its ground suits, near its weight, the newest included.

title: A Roxxen learns driving in the traces
why: Asked for: "Roxxen need to have the Driving trade and gain experience in it when pulling a large cart or wagon". Its one skill, and its level, is driving now: a go at what a tile teaches the driver for every tile a large cart or a wagon it is in the traces of goes into, on both sides; nothing standing, nothing out of the traces, nothing for the Orse beside it. Its driving counts where climbing does in the team's pace, and one that had climbing keeps its level as driving, in a saved game and on the island.

title: Riding and pulling teach climbing
why: Asked for: "fix it so riding and pulling teach climbing". Every tile gone into on the ground is a go of climbing at `haul_learn_of` its rise, the browser's `haulLearn`, to the mount under its rider and to every beast in a pulled cart's traces that keeps climbing there; a Cartling learns its driving and no climbing. Nothing standing, nothing at heel, more up a slope than on the flat.

title: Haulers take shoes, at half a mount's
why: Asked for: "Allow shoeing haulers at half bonus". A draught beast takes shoes as a mount does; in a vehicle's traces a shod one is worth `haul_shoe_share` of a mount's shoes at its share of the team, on the pace on laid stone and on the step, on both sides.

title: A repeated mould pour takes the first pour's metal
why: Reported: a pour from lower QL mithril in a wagon, repeated, took the pack's higher QL mithril. A repeat queued behind the pour names the wagon's stack, and is poured from it or refused: never a stand-in from the pack for a stack in a store, on both sides.

title: Climbing in the traces at a Wagonox's rate, level off the level skill
why: Asked of a Chiptail line levelling far quicker than a Wagonox in the same wagon: a tile in the traces teaches climbing at a Wagonox's base a tile pulled (`haul_learn` = `learns_gain_pull`), a steeper step proportionally more; and a creature's level and stage are its level skill's, the highest skill only for a kind with none. Both sides, and the migration's one-off step keeps every creature at the stage it had.

title: A bag worn carries more
why: Asked for: "Equipping a backpack increases weight held by up to 50%, a sack 25%. Both can be equipped and QL determines what % bonus they apply." Back and Side slots on both sides, the carry limit times one and each worn bag's share times its QL / 100, and nothing for one carried and not worn.

title: What a step costs the island, and that it is the same step
why: The pack weighed in one pass and the lookups a step asks planned once a session: the weight, the limit and the share the same numbers to the last bit as every thing weighs itself; no vehicle and no mount NULL, not a row of NULLs; every lookup plpgsql; and a step still goes where it is asked and stops short of the trees.

title: Where things come from, impossible things swept, and work faster than its pace
why: Asked for: modified-item detection. Every new row of the item table says what kind of door made it, the door and whose it was: a craft, a forage, a butchering, a deal, a part split off a stack, a migration and a straight insert. A sweep of `sweep_rows()` rows at a go flags each impossible kind -- QL, damage and count out of bounds, no such thing, QL past its maker's best, a rarity with no such rarity or no roll, no origin -- leaves good things and the island alone, and files one keeper report a holder. Only a keeper may hold a thing out of play and put it back. Goes due faster than any go can are a Work rate flag; goes at the pace, and a backlog settled at once, are not.

title: A settlement grown to Solara's size sends less
why: Counted, not timed, on a copy of the island filled to Solara's counts (tools/perf/sql): a thing lying about is sent in at most 110 bytes; asked again with nothing written, the crates are left out and no companion at heel is sent again, in at most 10 kB.

title: A wildermon in a crate keeps, and one at heel is not written again
why: Asked for: "When crated, everything except ages should freeze, and age only ticks once daily." Crated: hunger, health, care, fleece and age stage held over an island day and a half, settled once an island day, not born in the crate; let out after an hour, its pregnancy, meal bonus and bleed an hour later and its body from then. At heel with nothing changed: no row written.

title: A settlement grown to Solara's size draws less a frame
why: Counted, not timed, in Chrome on the page's own clock, with 30 other players in view: the buildings' kept pictures put down at most four screens of pixels a frame, and the sculpted bodies are drawn again at most four a frame, and your own.

title: The Bauble of Regret, and a trade undone
why: Asked for: a 3% chance of a Bauble of Regret in archaeology, which undoes a trade. Both sides turn one up as often, off the same roll as a tarnished bauble; breaking one puts the trade down with its tree or its perks, leaves the other slot alone, is refused in the browser's words, and the next trade in that slot costs nothing.

title: Perks, six tiers of three, and what each one does
why: Asked for: every class has six tiers, at 50 and then 60 to 100 in its main skill, and at each one choice of three. Both sides hold the same perks and fold them the same way; choosing is refused in the browser's words; the Trades window's tree is every tier with its three; every key a perk has is read by an island rule; and each of the Terraformer's eighteen does what its note says, measured where the rule is.

title: The Miner's perks, each where its rule is
why: Each of the Miner's eighteen measured on the island with the dice taken out where they can be: the face and what it asks, Chip corner, the trowel, and Pan; and the browser reading the same numbers where it draws or asks them.

title: Somebody else at mining is drawn with their own pickaxe, the same on both sides
why: Asked for: "other players are shown mining with their own pickaxe's metal", not iron. The island takes the job's tool from the pack as the job starts and at every go (player.act_tool) and says it in rpc_act's and rpc_settle's answers; one body mining with a copper pickaxe and then an enchanted gold one is read by another body on the island, signed in as them, as copper and then gold, enchanted: the same piece as the miner's own browser takes from the same pack, and the sculpted figure drawn with the head in that metal.

title: The Mason's perks, each where its rule is
why: Each of the Mason's eighteen measured on the island with the dice taken out where they can be: the chisel, the trowel, Repoint and Tall Walls, the rock and Rubble Fill, the stone arch; and the browser reading the same numbers where it asks or offers them.

title: The Carpenter's perks, each where its rule is
why: Each of the Carpenter's eighteen measured on the island with the dice taken out where they can be: the saw and the bench, the maker's mark on a chest, a boat, a cart and a bow and what each does with it, the bench wearing its tool and Saw Care halving it, fences, salvage and bridges; and the browser reading the same numbers.

title: Every smithing job takes a hammer
why: The island's smith_tool() is the browser's SMITH_TOOL; every mould is fired with it on both sides; pouring, casting an anvil, smithing, striking coins and fitting a padlock each refuse without it, in the browser's words; no other blacksmithing job goes without it.

title: Jobs that went without a tool take one
